subject: Cost guardrails & efficiency matrix for MAP / evaluation plan
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Jensen <beth.jensen@novushealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700 (PDT)
Subject: Cost guardrails & efficiency matrix for MAP / evaluation plan

Hi Beth —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised I attached a lightweight workbook (MAP Cost Workbook v1.xlsx) that ties the MAP milestones to explicit cost gating criteria and the short evaluation plan we discussed. High-level asks from our side so we can finalize the MAP and align timelines with procurement: 

- Confirm workload profile: avg tokens per call, 95th pct tokens, expected monthly calls (you gave 1.2M as a starting point — please confirm).
- HIPAA note: clarify whether any prefetching or offline caching of PHI is permissible under your DPA (we can propose encrypted KMS-backed cache if needed).
- Target close date: you mentioned a June 1 go-live goal — to hit that we'll need MAP sign-off by Apr 24 so SOW and procurement can queue the reserved capacity.

What we included in the workbook / evaluation plan:
- Two cost scenarios (conservative / aggressive) that vary on cache-hit and batching assumptions. Example assumptions are:
  * Conservative: cache hit 30%, steady-state batch size = 4, average request tokens = 650.
  * Aggressive: cache hit 60%, steady-state batch size = 12, average request tokens = 520.
- Simple tokens-per-dollar worked examples (see tab "efficiency-matrix"). These let you see the sensitivity to cache hit and batch size.
- Evaluation plan (48h functional run + 72h stress run) + gating: effective tokens per call target, 95th latency threshold, and end-to-end p50/p95 for your UI flows.

Next steps (my proposed):
1) You confirm the workload numbers and any PHI/caching constraints by Tue 4/14.
2) We run a 48-hour eval on a small reserved pool using your sample traffic (you can drop sample-traffic.jsonl into the shared folder).
3) We reconvene with results and finalize MAP sign-off by Apr 24 (if metrics meet gating).

Quick note on the model & cost arithmetic so you have context before we run numbers: the workbook uses per-1k-token pricing for the model family you selected plus an overhead line for KV/prefix cache misses (i.e., we bill only tokens generated/server-side; cache hits avoid model execution but we count a small storage/IO delta in the conservative scenario).

Attachments: MAP Cost Workbook v1.xlsx (calc tabs), latency-slo-examples.pdf (SLO framing), sample-traffic.jsonl (format sample).

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Beth Jensen <beth.jensen@novushealth.com>

Cc: Novus Health Procurement <procurement@novushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 08:40:00 -0700 (PDT)
Subject: Re: Cost guardrails & efficiency matrix for MAP / evaluation plan

Aditya —

Thanks for this and the workbook. Quick answers and a few clarifying questions: 

- Workload: confirmed 1.2M calls / month (avg). Token distributions: median ~420 tokens, mean ~550 tokens, 95th ~1,400 tokens. I pasted a small sample of anonymized requests into the shared folder.
- PHI/caching: our compliance team will not allow persistent prefetching of PHI outside our VPC. Short-term in-memory KV prefix caching in the service (ephemeral, encrypted) is acceptable.
- Timeline: procurement has an internal review on May 2; if MAP is signed by Apr 24 we can aim for June 1 SOW start.

Two questions we need answered before we sign off on the gating: 
1) How sensitive are monthly costs to cache-hit assumptions (30% vs 60%)? Can you show a concrete worked example?
2) If we enforce a 200–350ms p95 latency SLO, how does that constrain batching (we need to avoid introducing user-facing lag)?

If you can include the worked examples in the workbook and call out the gating thresholds clearly, we can circulate to procurement.

Best,
Beth
Director, Product Ops | Novus Health
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Jensen <beth.jensen@novushealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700 (PDT)
Subject: Re: Cost guardrails & efficiency matrix for MAP / evaluation plan

Beth —

Great questions. I expanded the workbook with a concrete worked example and pasted the relevant excerpt below for quick review (we'll include it in the shared sheet too). Assumptions for this example (conservative baseline):
- Monthly calls: 1,200,000
- Mean tokens per call: 550
- Model price (hosted family, inference): $0.020 per 1k tokens (example price used for sensitivity only)
- Cache hit rate: 30% (conservative)
- When cached: cost = storage/IO amortized (we model $0.002 per 1k logical tokens equivalent for bookkeeping)
- Batching: steady-state effective batch size = 4 (lower batching to preserve latency)

Worked example (conservative):
- Gross billed tokens if no caching = 1,200,000 calls * 550 tokens = 660,000,000 tokens = 660k k-tokens.
- Model cost (no cache) = 660k * $0.020 = $13,200
- With 30% cache hit: billed tokens = 660,000,000 * (1 - 0.30) = 462,000,000 tokens => 462k k-tokens => model cost $9,240
- Cache IO/storage overhead for hits (bookkeeping): 30% * 660k k-tokens * $0.002 = $396
- Effective monthly cost (model + cache overhead) = $9,240 + $396 = $9,636
- Effective tokens per $ = total useful tokens served / cost = 660,000,000 / 9,636 ≈ 68,480 tokens per dollar

Aggressive scenario (60% cache; batch size 12):
- Billed tokens = 660,000,000 * 0.40 = 264,000,000 tokens => 264k k-tokens => model cost $5,280
- Cache overhead = 60% * 660k k-tokens * $0.002 = $792
- Effective monthly cost = $6,072
- Effective tokens per $ ≈ 660,000,000 / 6,072 ≈ 108,700 tokens per dollar

Latency vs batching tradeoff:
- With our serving runtime we commonly see near-linear improvements in tokens/sec with larger batches, but p95 user-visible latency degrades. For your 200–350ms p95 target we recommend a steady-state batch size in the 3–6 range for the 13B-class model (this keeps p95 under ~320ms in our benchmarks with typical front-end RPC overhead).
- Operational option: use dual-lane routing in the MAP — a low-latency lane (batch size 1–4, slightly higher cost) for interactive UI flows, and a high-efficiency lane (larger batches, prefetch-friendly) for background workflows (summaries, indexing). The MAP can gate acceptance on the interactive lane only.

Gating suggestions for signoff (we'll formalize these in the MAP doc):
- Effective tokens-per-$ >= 55k (conservative pass) OR monthly model spend <= $11k
- Cache hit rate >= 35% on sample traffic (ephemeral, in-memory caching only per your compliance note)
- p95 latency (interactive lane) <= 350ms

I'll schedule the 48h eval once you confirm sample-traffic.jsonl is good and compliance is OK with the ephemeral cache approach. We can surface the eval run metrics directly into the workbook and annotate the rows that must pass before Apr 24 signoff.

Regards,
Aditya

Team —

Summary of where we are with Novus (they confirmed traffic sample + PHI constraint for ephemeral in-memory caching):
- Workload confirmed: 1.2M calls/month; mean 550 tokens; p95 1,400 tokens.
- Procurement target: MAP signoff by Apr 24 -> SOW sequence to secure reserved capacity for June 1 start.

Action items:
1) Hannah: provision a 48h test cluster (2x A100 equivalent reservation) and ensure KV cache is ephemeral + KMS encrypted. Tag cluster: redwood-novus-eval-0426. Owner: Hannah. Due: 2026-04-16 EOD.
2) Ben: create the evaluation dashboard in Grafana and add rows to the MAP sheet for pass/fail gating (metrics: effective tokens/$, cache hit %, p50/p95 latency). Link the dashboard to the MAP workbook. Due: 2026-04-17 midday.
3) I will run the initial smoke on sample-traffic.jsonl and send results to Beth & procurement.

Gating thresholds to implement in the dashboard:
- Effective tokens-per-$ >= 55,000 
- Cache hit >= 35% (on anonymized sample)
- p95 (interactive lane) <= 350ms

Notes: prioritize low-latency lane metrics for signoff. If we can't meet the 55k tokens/$ on the initial run, include a mitigation row with recommended quantization or larger reserved instance plan (we may propose a dedicated capacity discount in the MAP if unit economics require it).

I'll update the MAP Cost Workbook with the evaluation run template and link the dashboard when Ben is done.

Thanks —
Aditya
